title: Production monitoring
task_statement: Watch live quality, cost, and model versions against a baseline, and page a named owner when a line breaks. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Usage and cost monitoring
components.first_principle: Spend becomes a quality signal only when it is divided by completed tasks in the same view.

edges.label: poll at most once per minute

steps: Open the Usage and Cost pages in the Claude Console for a quick check.
Pull usage buckets from the Usage API for each model and workspace.
Choose the bucket size: 1m for near-real-time, 1h for daily patterns, 1d for reports.
Divide spend by completed tasks to get cost per completed task.
Cache dashboard results between polls to stay within the polling guidance.
Set an alert line on cost per completed task, with a named owner. (Inference)
pros: Usage fields and the Usage API report token counts by model, workspace, and tier.
The Cost API reports daily cost in USD.
Cached tokens appear in their own count, so the cache effect is visible.
cons: Usage and cost data can appear later than 5 minutes after a request.
The Cost API supports only daily buckets.
Claude Platform on AWS has no programmatic Usage and Cost endpoints.
use_when: Spend grows while the number of completed tasks stays flat.
A team sets a monthly budget for a workload.
A workspace or API key needs its own spend view.
do_not_use_when: A single request needs a cost figure, because the usage fields already give it. (Inference)
The team needs a daily cost report only, and the Cost API already covers it. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Track cost per completed task next to total spend.
constraints.combination: Set the budget alert on the per-task value. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Poll the Usage API no more than once per minute for sustained use.
Use the 1m bucket for up to 1,440 buckets in a near-real-time view.
constraints.combination: Use the 1d bucket for up to 31 buckets in a report.

constraints.choice: Filter usage by workspace and API key to assign spend to owners.

native_services.text: The programmatic Usage and Cost API endpoints are not currently available. Use the Usage and Cost pages in the Claude Console.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)
native_services.text: Only the usage endpoint is available. Call it with Google Cloud credentials. The only predefined IAM role that allows the call is roles/claude.admin.

components.exam_tie: D4.6. Expect a scenario where spend looks stable but outcomes fall. The credited answer watches cost per completed task with a named alert owner. (Inference)
components.trap: A dashboard of total tokens with no completed-task count. Total spend looks normal while the outcome rate falls.
components.decision_rule: Show spend next to completed tasks, and alert on the per-task line.
components.exam_tip: A cost alert with no owner is a notification, not a control. (Inference)

components.name: Traces and telemetry
components.first_principle: A trace shows the order and timing of each hop in one request, which logs alone do not show.
steps: Add an OpenTelemetry destination in the Claude Console for API spans.
Choose the content mode for each destination that your data rules allow.
Set up SDK tracing for each client that sends Claude requests.
Read the trace of a failed or slow request to find the hop that failed.
Build eval cases from real traces when the destination stores full content.
pros: Traces cover Messages API requests, tool uses, and Managed Agents sessions.
Full content shows prompts and responses for each span.
Admins control the destinations, and developers can view them.
cons: Full content stores prompts and responses in the observability platform.
HIPAA, FERPA, and K-12 restrictions limit each destination to metadata.
API tracing works only on Claude Platform and Claude Platform on AWS, and OpenTelemetry export is in beta.
use_when: A team needs per-hop evidence for a failed or slow request.
A team builds an eval set from real production requests.
Several services must share one trace for each user request.
do_not_use_when: The data rules forbid content and metadata alone cannot answer the question. (Inference)
The API spans are needed on Amazon Bedrock, Claude Models on Google Cloud, or Microsoft Foundry, which the docs do not list for API tracing.
One log line answers the question, so no trace is needed. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Assign the admin role to the person who adds destinations.
constraints.combination: Give developers view access to the destinations.

constraints.choice: Shorten the Claude Code export interval only during a fault check.
constraints.combination: Reset the interval to the default for production use.

constraints.choice: Use metadata-only export when HIPAA, FERPA, or K-12 restrictions apply.
constraints.combination: Check the retention settings of the observability platform for full content.

constraints.choice: Set a maximum content size per span for full content destinations.

native_services.text: API tracing is supported in beta on Claude Platform on AWS. SDK tracing supports any cloud platform.

components.exam_tie: D4.6. Expect a scenario where a multi-step fault cannot be located from application logs. The credited answer uses per-hop traces for the request that broke. (Inference)
components.trap: Application logs alone. They record events, but they do not show the order and timing of each hop.
components.decision_rule: Add a destination per data rule, and choose the content mode that the rule allows.
components.exam_tip: Full content gives the most detail, and it stores prompts and responses in the destination.

components.name: Model version lock and drift
components.first_principle: A pinned model ID fixes the weights, so a behavior shift points to infrastructure, prompts, or data.

nodes.label: Dateless model ID as pinned snapshot

steps: Use the dateless model ID for the 4.6 generation and later.
Note the deprecation and retirement schedule for each model ID in use.
Keep a baseline of live metrics from before each model change.
Compare live metrics with the baseline after an infrastructure update.
Check prompt and data changes before you blame the model. (Inference)
Test a new model ID on the eval set before you change the production ID. (Inference)
pros: A dateless ID for the 4.6 generation and later maps to one fixed snapshot.
Each model ID has a deprecation schedule, so teams can plan migrations.
A model ID change appears in the request, so the change is visible.
cons: Infrastructure updates can shift behavior even when the model ID stays the same.
Aliases for earlier models move to the newest snapshot of that minor version.
A retirement date forces a migration on the schedule of that ID.
use_when: Behavior changed on a stable model ID with no code change.
A team plans a model migration and needs a baseline.
A quality line moved without a prompt or data change.
do_not_use_when: The shift has a known prompt or data change, so diagnosis comes first. (Inference)
The monitor covers a model that the production system does not use. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Record the model ID with every request and every metric.
constraints.combination: Compare the model ID in each metric with the release log. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Track the deprecation date of each model ID in the release plan.
Use a dated snapshot ID for earlier models when fixed behavior matters.
constraints.combination: Use an alias only when the team accepts moves to the newest snapshot. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Assign one owner to read model deprecation notices. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D4.6. Expect a scenario where behavior shifts on an unchanged model ID. The credited answer compares live metrics with the baseline before it changes the model. (Inference)
components.trap: A belief that a model ID guarantees identical output at all times. The weights stay fixed, but infrastructure updates can shift observable behavior.
components.decision_rule: Pin the model ID, keep a baseline, and compare live metrics with that baseline after each change.
components.exam_tip: A stable model ID does not rule out a behavior shift from infrastructure.

key_facts.text: For the 4.6 generation and later, the dateless model ID maps to a single fixed snapshot.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Anthropic does not update the weights or configuration of a released model ID.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Every model ID, dated or dateless, has its own deprecation and retirement schedule.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Infrastructure updates can cause minor differences in behavior even when the model ID and weights do not change.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Aliases for earlier models point to the most recent dated snapshot for that minor version.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Live metric below its line?} -->|No| X[No action needed]
  A -->|Yes| B{Offline eval set also dropped?}
  B -->|No| C[Refresh eval set from production samples]
  B -->|Yes| D{Model ID changed?}
  D -->|Yes| E[Compare with pinned baseline]
  D -->|No| F[Check prompt and data changes]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  U[Usage and Cost API] --> C[Cost per completed task]
  O[OpenTelemetry traces] --> H[Per-hop evidence]
  H --> D[Diagnosis]
  M[Pinned model ID] --> B[Baseline]
  B --> L[Alert line]
  L --> P[Named owner]
  O --> E[Eval cases from traces]

patterns.wording: usage totals rise while completed tasks stay flat
patterns.answer_type: cost per completed task line with an owner
patterns.rule: Show spend next to completed tasks, and alert on the per-task line with a named owner.
traps: Cut the model tier before the data check

patterns.wording: live quality slides while the offline eval set still scores well
patterns.answer_type: alert with a refreshed production sample
patterns.rule: Page the named owner, then refresh the eval set from production samples.
traps: Roll back the model tier before diagnosis

patterns.wording: behavior shifts on a stable model ID with no code change
patterns.rule: Compare live metrics with the baseline, then check prompts, data, and the model ID.
traps: Assume a model ID fixes all output
Change the prompt before the evidence
